1	// Package gitremote provides general-purpose git remote URL utilities:
2	// parsing, resolving, and redacting remote URLs. It has no dependency on
3	// checkpoint, strategy, or settings packages.
4	package gitremote
5	
6	import (
7		"context"
8		"errors"
9		"fmt"
10		"net/url"
11		"os/exec"
12		"strings"
13		"unicode"
14	)
15	
16	const (
17		ProtocolSSH   = "ssh"
18		ProtocolHTTPS = "https"
19		// ProtocolEntire is the scheme of Entire's git remote helper (entire://).
20		// These URLs carry a forge/namespace prefix before owner/repo.
21		ProtocolEntire = "entire"
22	)
23	
24	// Info holds the parsed components of a git remote URL.
25	// Host is the hostname only (never includes a port). Port is empty unless the
26	// source URL specified an explicit non-default port. Callers that need the
27	// combined "host[:port]" form should use HostPort.
28	//
29	// Forge is the short identifier of the upstream forge ("gh", "et", ...) used
30	// by the Entire trails API. It is populated from the path prefix on entire://
31	// URLs (entire://host/<forge>/owner/repo) and from a hostname lookup on
32	// direct git URLs (github.com → "gh"). It is empty for direct git URLs to
33	// unrecognized hosts, and for entire:// URLs without a forge segment.
34	type Info struct {
35		Protocol string
36		Host     string
37		Port     string
38		Forge    string
39		Owner    string
40		Repo     string
41	}
42	
43	// hostToForge maps direct git hostnames to their forge identifier on the
44	// trails API. entire:// URLs carry the forge in the path instead and bypass
45	// this map.
46	var hostToForge = map[string]string{
47		"github.com": "gh",
48	}
49	
50	// forgeToHost is the reverse of hostToForge: it maps a forge identifier back to
51	// its canonical public host. Used to recover the real forge host from an
52	// entire:// remote, whose Host is the Entire cluster rather than the forge.
53	var forgeToHost = func() map[string]string {
54		m := make(map[string]string, len(hostToForge))
55		for host, forge := range hostToForge {
56			m[forge] = host
57		}
58		return m
59	}()
60	
61	// IsSupportedForge reports whether forge is a known short forge id (e.g. "gh")
62	// understood by the trails API. It rejects forge hostnames ("github.com") and
63	// any other unrecognized value, so callers parsing a bare forge/owner/repo
64	// triple can fail clearly instead of forwarding a malformed forge to the API.
65	func IsSupportedForge(forge string) bool {
66		_, ok := forgeToHost[forge]
67		return ok
68	}
69	
70	// CanonicalHost returns the canonical public host of the upstream forge.
71	//
72	// For direct git URLs this is just Host. For entire:// remotes — whose Host is
73	// the Entire cluster (e.g. aws-us-east-2.entire.io) rather than the forge — it
74	// maps the forge prefix back to the forge's host (gh → github.com). Falls back
75	// to Host when the forge is unknown (e.g. a self-hosted GitHub Enterprise),
76	// preserving the only host we know for it.
77	func (i *Info) CanonicalHost() string {
78		if host, ok := forgeToHost[i.Forge]; ok {
79			return host
80		}
81		return i.Host
82	}
83	
84	// HostPort returns Host, or "Host:Port" when Port is non-empty.
85	func (i *Info) HostPort() string {
86		if i.Port == "" {
87			return i.Host
88		}
89		return i.Host + ":" + i.Port
90	}
91	
92	// GetRemoteURL returns the URL configured for the named git remote.
93	func GetRemoteURL(ctx context.Context, remoteName string) (string, error) {
94		return GetRemoteURLInDir(ctx, "", remoteName)
95	}
96	
97	// GetRemoteURLInDir returns the URL configured for the named git remote in dir.
98	func GetRemoteURLInDir(ctx context.Context, dir, remoteName string) (string, error) {
99		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "remote", "get-url", remoteName)
100		if dir != "" {
101			cmd.Dir = dir
102		}
103		output, err := cmd.Output()
104		if err != nil {
105			return "", fmt.Errorf("remote %q not found", remoteName)
106		}
107		return strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), nil
108	}

29	// gitHookContext holds common state for git hook logging.
30	type gitHookContext struct {
31		hookName string
32		ctx      context.Context
33		span     *perf.Span
34		strategy *strategy.ManualCommitStrategy
35	}

37	// newGitHookContext creates a new git hook context with logging and a root perf span.
38	// The perf span ensures all perf.Start calls in strategy methods become child spans,
39	// producing a single perf log line per hook with a full timing breakdown.
40	// Callers must defer g.span.End() to emit the perf log.
41	func newGitHookContext(ctx context.Context, hookName string) *gitHookContext {
42		ctx = logging.WithComponent(ctx, "hooks")
43		ctx, span := perf.Start(ctx, hookName,
44			slog.String("hook_type", "git"))
45		g := &gitHookContext{
46			hookName: hookName,
47			ctx:      ctx,
48			span:     span,
49		}
50		g.strategy = GetStrategy(ctx)
51		return g
52	}

54	// logInvoked logs that the hook was invoked.
55	func (g *gitHookContext) logInvoked(extraAttrs ...any) {
56		attrs := []any{
57			slog.String("hook", g.hookName),
58			slog.String("hook_type", "git"),
59			slog.String("strategy", strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit),
60		}
61		logging.Debug(g.ctx, g.hookName+" hook invoked", append(attrs, extraAttrs...)...)
62	}

64	// logCompleted records the error on the perf span.
65	func (g *gitHookContext) logCompleted(err error) {
66		g.span.RecordError(err)
67	}

69	func (g *gitHookContext) skipUnsupportedCheckpointPolicy() bool {
70		// Callers return success when this is true because policy failures should
71		// disable Entire checkpoint work, not make Git reject the user's operation.
72		repo, err := gitrepo.OpenCurrent(g.ctx)
73		if err != nil {
74			return g.skipUnreadableCheckpointPolicy(err)
75		}
76		defer repo.Close()
77	
78		state, err := checkpointpolicy.ReadLocal(g.ctx, repo)
79		if err != nil {
80			return g.skipUnreadableCheckpointPolicy(err)
81		}
82	
83		policy := state.Policy
84		if checkpointpolicy.CanSatisfyPolicy(policy) {
85			return false
86		}
87	
88		logging.Warn(g.ctx, "checkpoint policy unsupported; skipping git hook",
89			slog.String("checkpoint_version", policy.CheckpointVersion),
90			slog.String("checkpoint_min_version", policy.CheckpointMinVersion))
91		if interactive.CanPromptInteractively() {
92			fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, checkpointpolicy.UnsupportedPolicyMessage(
93				policy,
94				versioncheck.UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary(versioninfo.Version),
95			))
96		}
97		emitCheckpointPolicyBlocked(g.ctx, telemetry.CheckpointPolicyBlockedEvent{
98			Hook:                 g.hookName,
99			HookType:             telemetry.PolicyBlockedHookTypeGit,
100			Reason:               telemetry.PolicyBlockedReasonUnsupported,
101			Outcome:              telemetry.PolicyBlockedOutcomeSkipped,
102			CheckpointVersion:    policy.CheckpointVersion,
103			CheckpointMinVersion: policy.CheckpointMinVersion,
104		})
105		return true
106	}
107	
108	// skipUnreadableCheckpointPolicy warns, notifies the user, and reports the
109	// policy-blocked telemetry event for a hook whose checkpoint policy could not be
110	// read. It always returns true so callers skip Entire checkpoint work.
111	func (g *gitHookContext) skipUnreadableCheckpointPolicy(err error) bool {
112		logging.Warn(g.ctx, "checkpoint policy read failed; skipping git hook",
113			slog.String("error", err.Error()))
114		if interactive.CanPromptInteractively() {
115			fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "[entire] Could not read checkpoint policy; skipping Entire checkpoint work: %v\n", err)
116		}
117		emitCheckpointPolicyBlocked(g.ctx, telemetry.CheckpointPolicyBlockedEvent{
118			Hook:     g.hookName,
119			HookType: telemetry.PolicyBlockedHookTypeGit,
120			Reason:   telemetry.PolicyBlockedReasonUnreadable,
121			Outcome:  telemetry.PolicyBlockedOutcomeSkipped,
122		})
123		return true
124	}

126	// initHookLogging initializes logging for hooks by finding the most recent session.
127	// Returns a cleanup function that should be deferred.
128	// If Entire is not set up or disabled, returns a no-op to avoid creating files.
129	func initHookLogging(ctx context.Context) func() {
130		// Don't create any files if Entire is not active for this repo
131		// (repo-level setup or the user-global tier). This is checked here as
132		// defense-in-depth (also checked in PersistentPreRunE); both layers of
133		// the gate must use the same predicate, settings.IsActiveForRepo, so
134		// global-mode repos get hook logging and redaction configuration too.
135		if !settings.IsActiveForRepo(ctx) {
136			return func() {}
137		}
138	
139		// Set up log level getter so logging can read from settings
140		logging.SetLogLevelGetter(GetLogLevel)
141	
142		// Read session ID for the slog attribute (empty string is fine - log file is fixed)
143		sessionID := strategy.FindMostRecentSession(ctx)
144		if err := logging.Init(ctx, sessionID); err != nil {
145			// Init failed - logging will use stderr fallback
146			return func() {}
147		}
148	
149		// Configure redaction once at startup: PII (opt-in), inline custom_redactions,
150		// and rule packs discovered under .entire/redactors/. No-op if nothing is configured.
151		strategy.EnsureRedactionConfigured()
152	
153		return logging.Close
154	}

160	func newHooksGitCmd() *cobra.Command {
161		cmd := &cobra.Command{
162			Use:    "git",
163			Short:  "Git hook handlers",
164			Long:   "Commands called by git hooks. These delegate to the current strategy.",
165			Hidden: true, // Internal command, not for direct user use
166			PersistentPreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
167				ctx := cmd.Context()
168				// Check if Entire is active for this repo before doing any work.
169				// This prevents global git hooks from doing anything in repos
170				// where Entire was never enabled (repo-level or via the
171				// user-global tier) or has been disabled.
172				if !settings.IsActiveForRepo(ctx) {
173					gitHooksDisabled = true
174					return nil
175				}
176				// Discover external agent plugins so GetByAgentType works correctly
177				// during condensation (e.g. post-commit). Without this, external agents
178				// registered in the hook phase cannot be resolved here, causing token
179				// usage and other agent-specific data to be missing from metadata.json.
180				discoveryCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5*time.Second)
181				defer cancel()
182				external.DiscoverAndRegister(discoveryCtx)
183				hookLogCleanup = initHookLogging(ctx)
184				return nil
185			},
186			PersistentPostRunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
187				if hookLogCleanup != nil {
188					hookLogCleanup()
189				}
190				return nil
191			},

@@ -3,6 +3,7 @@ package gitremote
 import (
 	"context"
 	"os/exec"
+	"path/filepath"
 	"testing"
 
 	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/testutil"
@@ -258,3 +259,73 @@ func TestResolveRemoteRepo_MissingRemote(t *testing.T) {
 	_, _, _, err := ResolveRemoteRepo(context.Background(), "origin")
 	assert.Error(t, err)
 }
+
+func TestGetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	newRepo := func(t *testing.T) string {
+		t.Helper()
+		dir := t.TempDir()
+		testutil.InitRepo(t, dir)
+		return dir
+	}
+	runGit := func(t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) {
+		t.Helper()
+		cmd := exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), "git", args...)
+		cmd.Dir = dir
+		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
+		require.NoError(t, cmd.Run())
+	}
+
+	t.Run("remote configured", func(t *testing.T) {
+		t.Parallel()
+		dir := newRepo(t)
+		runGit(t, dir, "remote", "add", "origin", "git@github.com:acme/widgets.git")
+
+		urls, found, err := GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet(t.Context(), dir, "origin")
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		assert.True(t, found)
+		assert.Equal(t, []string{"git@github.com:acme/widgets.git"}, urls)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("multiple URLs are all returned", func(t *testing.T) {
+		t.Parallel()
+		dir := newRepo(t)
+		runGit(t, dir, "remote", "add", "origin", "git@github.com:acme/widgets.git")
+		runGit(t, dir, "remote", "set-url", "--add", "origin", "https://github.com/acme/mirror.git")
+
+		urls, found, err := GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet(t.Context(), dir, "origin")
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		assert.True(t, found)
+		assert.Equal(t, []string{"git@github.com:acme/widgets.git", "https://github.com/acme/mirror.git"}, urls)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("remote not configured is found=false, not an error", func(t *testing.T) {
+		t.Parallel()
+		dir := newRepo(t)
+
+		urls, found, err := GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet(t.Context(), dir, "origin")
+		require.NoError(t, err)
+		assert.False(t, found)
+		assert.Empty(t, urls)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("lookup failure is an error, not found=false", func(t *testing.T) {
+		t.Parallel()
+		dir := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "does-not-exist")
+
+		_, _, err := GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet(t.Context(), dir, "origin")
+		assert.Error(t, err)
+	})
+
+	t.Run("canceled context is an error even with a configured remote", func(t *testing.T) {
+		t.Parallel()
+		dir := newRepo(t)
+		runGit(t, dir, "remote", "add", "origin", "git@github.com:acme/widgets.git")
+
+		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(t.Context())
+		cancel()
+		_, _, err := GetRemoteURLsInDirIfSet(ctx, dir, "origin")
+		assert.Error(t, err)
+	})
+}

83	// getHookType returns the hook type based on the hook name.
84	// Returns "subagent" for task-related hooks (pre-task, post-task, post-todo),
85	// "tool" for tool-related hooks (before-tool, after-tool),
86	// "agent" for all other agent hooks.
87	func getHookType(hookName string) string {
88		switch hookName {
89		case claudecode.HookNamePreTask, claudecode.HookNamePostTask, claudecode.HookNamePostTodo:
90			return "subagent"
91		case geminicli.HookNameBeforeTool, geminicli.HookNameAfterTool:
92			return "tool"
93		default:
94			return "agent"
95		}
96	}
97	
98	// executeAgentHook runs the core hook execution logic for a given agent and hook name.
99	// It handles git repo checks, enabled checks, logging, event parsing, and lifecycle dispatch.
100	// Used by both the registered subcommand path and the RunE fallback for external agents.
101	// When initLogging is true, it initializes and cleans up hook logging (used by the RunE fallback
102	// since it doesn't go through PersistentPreRunE). Built-in agent subcommands pass false since
103	// their parent command's PersistentPreRunE already handles logging.
104	func executeAgentHook(cmd *cobra.Command, agentName types.AgentName, hookName string, initLogging bool) error {
105		// Skip silently if not in a git repository - hooks shouldn't prevent the agent from working
106		worktreeRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(cmd.Context())
107		if err != nil {
108			return nil
109		}
110	
111		// Skip if Entire is not set up and enabled. This must fail closed: any
112		// settings read error (missing file, corrupted JSON, transient I/O
113		// failure) is treated as disabled so a hook never silently falls through
114		// to full lifecycle work just because settings couldn't be read. Using
115		// IsEnabled here previously failed OPEN on error (`err == nil && !enabled`
116		// only short-circuits when the read succeeded), which meant a corrupted
117		// or unreadable settings file made every hook invocation pay the full
118		// dispatch cost instead of exiting fast (#524).
119		// settings.IsActiveForRepo is the same fail-closed gate the git hooks
120		// use (see PersistentPreRunE in hooks_git_cmd.go). It extends
121		// IsSetUpAndEnabled with the user-global tier: repos with no repo-level
122		// setup proceed when global mode is on and the repo is not excluded.
123		if !settings.IsActiveForRepo(cmd.Context()) {
124			return nil
125		}
126	
127		if initLogging {
128			cleanup := initHookLogging(cmd.Context())
129			defer cleanup()
130		}
131	
132		// Initialize logging context with agent name
133		ctx := logging.WithAgent(logging.WithComponent(cmd.Context(), "hooks"), agentName)
134	
135		// Strategy name for logging
136		strategyName := strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit
137
